# PCA

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/trippzac/PCA/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/trippzac/PCA/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/trippzac/PCA/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/trippzac/PCA)
<!-- badges: end -->

## Overview

The goal of PCA is to recreate the functionality of built-in functions for principal component analysis using my own code. Specifically, we provide two functions `PCA()` and `PCA_using_SVD()` that implement principal component analysis by computing eigenvectors and by computing singular values respectively. These are analogous to how each of the two built-in functions `prcomp()` and `princomp()` work (though we compare both of our functions to `prcomp()` for simplicity of testing). Additionally, we provide two additional functions `variance_explained_by_PCA()` and `scree_plot()` to help the user analyze which principal components they may wish to keep in their analysis. These functions are analogous to the functions found in the library "factoextra".

## Installation

You can install the development version of PCA like so:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
devtools::install_github("trippzac/PCA", build_vignettes = T)
```

## Usage

This is a basic example of how to use PCA. Its use and output is similar to that
of the built-in function `prcomp()`

```{r}
library(PCA)
set.seed(17)
y <- matrix(rnorm(101*10), 101, 10)
PCA(y)

PCA_using_SVD(y)

variance_explained_by_PCA(y)

scree_plot(y)
```

We include one more example where there is slight numerical differences between our two functions for illustrative purposes.

```{r}
z <- matrix(1:24, ncol = 3)
PCA(z)
PCA_using_SVD(z)
```


Notice the difference in the numerical precision for the second eigenvector and the fact that the eigenvectors may be in a different order. The function `PCA_using_SVD()` appears to numerically match the results from `prcomp()`, and it appears to always choose the eigenvectors in the same order and with the same sign as well, making it easier to make a baseline comparison between the functions. 


## Getting Help

There are further examples in the help pages and in the vignettes of using these functions. Additionally, we perform benchmarking there as well to compare the speed of `PCA_using_SVD()` to `prcomp()`.
